description: Prospective synthetic specification and refusal challenge; not independently authored or blinded.

cases.question: For an exploratory 84-participant single-arm study, calculate Bayesian assurance. The response target is 36%, the minimum is 21%, and higher response is better. Use treatment prior Beta(2,3), target gate 0.85, minimum gate 0.90, and stop gate 0.10.

Calculate Bayesian assurance for an exploratory single-arm study of 110 participants. A previous study observed 6 responses in 18 patients. The response target is 43%, the minimum is 24%, and higher response is better. Set the target gate to 0.75, the minimum gate to 0.88, and the stop gate to 0.05.

Calculate Bayesian assurance for a randomized exploratory trial with 140 participants total. The control response rate is 42%. The desired treatment benefit is 12 percentage points and the minimum benefit is 3 percentage points. A treatment pilot had 9 responses in 30 patients; use Beta(2,3) as the control analysis prior. Set target, minimum, and stop gates to 0.78, 0.91, and 0.07 respectively.

For an exploratory Bayesian interim calculation, 8 of 25 patients responded in a planned 96-patient single-arm study. The target response rate is 33%, the minimum is 19%, and higher response is better. Use Beta(3,2) as the prior and gates 0.82, 0.92, and 0.08 for target, minimum, and stop, respectively.

Calculate Bayesian assurance for an exploratory 72-person single-arm trial with target response 37%, minimum 22%, and decision gates 0.81, 0.93, and 0.09 for target, minimum, and stop. No prior distribution or previous-study data are available.
Calculate Bayesian assurance for an exploratory 66-person single-arm trial with target response 38%, minimum 23%, and prior Beta(2,4). No decision gates have been specified.
Calculate Bayesian assurance for an exploratory 78-person single-arm trial with target response 39%, minimum 17%, and Beta(0,2) prior. The target, minimum, and stop gates are 0.81, 0.94, and 0.06.
Estimate time to first readmission with death as a competing risk, using a Fine-Gray model.
